requirement: Facility, Tenant, and Organization identifiers remain stable through rename, transfer, restructuring, and closure.
Facility, Tenant, Organization, Barn, and Business remain distinct concepts and are never silently aliased.
Every tenant-scoped object, request, event, job, cache, export, search record, and offline bundle is bound to exactly one tenant unless an explicit cross-tenant contract applies.
Organization-to-Tenant control is explicit, temporal, evidenced, and non-permission-bearing by itself.
Tenant-to-Facility association is explicit, temporal, purpose-scoped, and does not expose tenant-private projections to another tenant.
Facility containment and non-containment topology are modeled separately with effective dates and lineage.
Aliases, historical names, splits, merges, and relocations preserve prior references and provenance.
Facility association, organization type, role label, employment, lease, payment, contact, profile, ownership claim, or stewardship claim never independently grants permission.
Membership, staff assignment, representation, delegation, and guardianship remain Relationship-domain facts.
Permission decisions remain owned by Permission and consume only referenced, current topology facts.
The active tenant and applicable facility are continuously visible to the actor.
Every context switch records actor chain, prior and new context, reason, timestamp, session, device, and result.
Server authorization binds the selected tenant, facility, context version, principal, permission version, and resource scope; caller-supplied IDs never override it.
Tenant, facility, or organization suspension is enforced across online, API, search, exports, jobs, support, and integrations.
Offline access expires and stale bundles cannot authorize consequential writes after suspension, context change, or authority revocation.
Support and representation preserve the authenticated human actor and represented principal; silent impersonation is prohibited.
Facility, Organization, Tenant, people, horses, and precise location are private and non-discoverable by default.
Public facility discovery uses a separate minimal projection with field-level authority, revocation, freshness, and anti-enumeration controls.
Search, autocomplete, error behavior, counts, timing, and exports do not reveal cross-tenant existence.
Precise facility location, security systems, minor-associated areas, animal location, hazards, and emergency resources receive sensitive treatment.
Facility transfer or operator change never automatically transfers horses, private records, relationships, agreements, invoices, permissions, credentials, or evidence.
Organization, Tenant, or Facility merge and split operations never cascade into unrelated identities or downstream domain merges.
Duplicate detection preserves uncertainty and no merge is automatic or based only on name, address, payment, contact, or shared user.
Ambiguous legacy topology remains quarantined, tenant-scoped, non-public, non-authority-bearing, attributable, and reviewable.
Timezone uses an IANA identifier; locale uses BCP 47; postal and geospatial representations retain source, precision, confidence, and effective time.
Every material topology fact records provenance, confidence or verification state, effective time, and responsible actor.
Every material lifecycle, context, topology, duplicate, public-projection, support, and reconciliation event is auditable and tamper-evident according to Audit canon.
Closure and archival preserve required historical identity and references while ending ordinary current visibility and access.
Recovery and replay never resurrect closed, suspended, expired, merged, or revoked context or access.
Every API query and mutation enforces authoritative tenant scope before object lookup and returns non-enumerating errors.
Events carry event ID, schema version, tenant, entity, effective time, actor chain, provenance, and idempotency key.
Jobs are tenant-partitioned, checkpointed, idempotent, permission-aware, suspendable, and prevent cross-tenant aggregation unless separately authorized.
Derived indexes and caches are tenant-segmented and receive priority invalidation for suspension, closure, revocation, transfer, and public-projection change.
Current barn/account compatibility fields are treated only as as-built mirrors and never as the final Facility/Tenant/Organization model.
First-user seeding does not create organization, membership, relationship, role, permission, or authority facts unless their owning domain separately authorizes them.
Provider, vendor, and service organization actions preserve organization identity, temporal relationship, agreement reference, and accountable human actor where known.
Stewardship assertions remain distinct from ownership, custody, payment, contact, relationship, and permission and retain evidence and dispute state.
Facility, Tenant, and Organization lifecycle state machines use explicit permitted transitions, evidence, approval, notice handoff, audit, and reconciliation.
Data collection and public or cross-tenant processing are purpose-limited and minimum-necessary.
No document in this package authorizes implementation, schema change, migration, database mutation, application startup, deployment, enrollment, or production use.
